limitations: Independent review checked all 56 file hashes and canonical package root, the 22 theorem/type/claim inventory entries, exact Audit generation, model, registered runner, contract and experiment design. Two gated clean builds were not executed by this reviewer. Approval is an implementation-contract decision, not mechanical proof discharge or runtime acceptance.

The fixed package-private profile, document=false rejection, DEFAULT constructors, immutable profile and non-DEFAULT revalidate guard provide a concrete narrow implementation boundary. Actual DocumentQueries.validate is the advisory construction site; DocumentMutations uses DocumentWorker::new for both commit validation and history revalidation, while JobService uses the default solver launcher. These callsite and default behaviors must be mechanically checked in the final patch and compiled inventory; package privacy alone does not prove authority separation.

Actual BubblewrapLauncher constructor checks full BuildIdentity, and launch checks Alloy plus full BuildIdentity before clearing the environment and starting its sandbox. Actual DocumentWorker and FrameProcess preserve bounded frames, nonce checks and finally-based child reaping. The runtime argv comparator must establish every complete baseline argument and exact single-option insertion; the Lean RequiredArgs placeholder proves only syntactic equalities under that extraction.

Fresh-process lifecycle and selection theorems trust identity checks, observed reap and run measurements. The unchanged durable field is abstract; neither it nor guarded Step constructors prove JVM semantics, Java correspondence, kernel confinement, cleanup timing or universal response equality. The hypothetical selection witness is not a measured performance result.

Complete private-response equality and typed generated-ID normalization are appropriately stronger than status comparison. Runtime implementation must validate injective kind-preserving mappings, preserve existing IDs, source bytes/hash and diagnostics, and reject topology swaps and UUID-looking literals. Concrete fixture bytes, independent oracle/comparator negative cases and verifier hashes remain mandatory before execution; no comparator has yet passed.

All three paired whole-stack runs must independently satisfy 500 nodes, 100 warmups, 1000 measurements, zero errors, strict p95 below 300 ms, memory at most 5 GiB, and strict paired improvement. The 240 ms figure is headroom only. Three measured pairs provide finite selection evidence, not a universal speedup or statistical confidence claim.

The 4-CPU quota and 6-GiB workstation ceiling are screening conditions, not intended 4-vCPU/8-GiB host acceptance. Effective cgroup ownership and descendant cleanup must be observed, and uncontained fallbacks are prohibited. Existing P1 safety/availability limitations persist; the same approved P1 implementation must be held fixed across variants.

Approval does not release the scheduling hold or authorize uncontrolled production rollout. Concrete frozen runtime manifests, safety/differential success, final patch/argv/callsite checks, every selection gate and explicit experiment scheduling remain required. F0 remains selected on any failure.

commercialization.reason: The contract makes no commercial-release claim. Target-host acceptance, customer/browser/security gates and Alloy/dependency redistribution obligations remain separate and open; an advisory compiler-option speedup cannot close them.
